# HackMusic: product reference

HackMusic turns a shared playlist into a lightweight social game for roughly 6–30 people at a house party, board-game night, or hackathon. Events typically run for 3–12 hours. The product is intended for closed, in-person gatherings rather than public music distribution.

## Experience

The host creates a room at https://hackmusic.fun, chooses its music source (Spotify or YouTube, locked for the whole event), and connects the host device to the event speaker. Spotify rooms play full tracks through the host's Spotify Premium account; YouTube rooms play videos on the host screen with no account required. A room can begin immediately or open first as a pre-party lobby. In lobby mode, guests can join early and submit secret Spotify or YouTube tracks, but playback and reactions stay locked until the host explicitly starts the event. The displayed schedule is informational and never auto-starts music. Guests open the invite URL, register a display name, and submit links from the room's service (Spotify track links, or YouTube video links including youtu.be and Shorts) without seeing the queue. Links from the other service are rejected. Playback stays on the host device.

During each song, guests can do nothing, cheer, or boo. A cheer produces a short happy sound over playback and gives the submitter 3 points. A boo produces a funny sound, removes 3 points from the submitter, and stays anonymous in the participant interface. Three boos skip to the next song. The event feed keeps the full history of songs and reactions.

The host can see and manage the waiting queue, enable reaction sounds, prevent the phone from sleeping when supported, skip songs, select a queue strategy, and end the party after confirmation. Queue strategies include submitted order, pure random selection, and a fair-ish shuffle that rotates among participants while preserving uncertainty.

The home page keeps a browser-local list of rooms created on that device, with quick links back to host controls. This shortcut history is not an account and disappears if the browser's site data is cleared.

HackMusic has a separate, unlinked read-only owner dashboard. It requires ChatGPT sign-in and a server-side owner email allowlist, is excluded from indexing, never returns host keys, and keeps boo identities anonymous.

## Product principles

- Fun and understandable within seconds.
- One shared speaker, many lightweight browser clients.
- Secret queue contents preserve surprise.
- Visible cheers create recognition; anonymous boos reduce social friction.
- Private event routes and host controls should not be indexed.
- No participant installation is required.

## Public canonical URL

https://hackmusic.fun/
